newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Placer says unable to look at Busang.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Placer says unable to look at Busang.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc said on Wednesday that it was frustrated that it had been unable to take a first hand look at the Busang gold deposit in Indonesia and has had to base decisions for its US$5 billion merger proposal with Bre-X Minerals Ltd on public information.

"We haven't really been able to visit the property and really understand what it is all about," Placer Dome's chief financial officer, Ian Austin, told a news briefing. "We've had to base all our decisions on public information," he said.
Placer Dome has proposed a merger Bre-X under which Indonesian interests would get a 40 percent interest in Busang, regarded as one of the world's largest untapped gold finds.

Austin said Placer had been preparing a team to perform due diligence work at the deposit in December, but that plan was cancelled by Bre-X. "They didn't fee comfortable with us on the property at that time," Austin told Reuters.
Bre-X found the Busang property, located in the Kalimantan province on Borneo island.
It is estimated by Bre-X to contain at least 57 million ounces of gold, currently worth over US$21 billion.
"There is a level of frustration there ... you're trying to make educated guesses rather than actually be able and see what is there," Austin said.
Placer's merger proposal followed an earlier alliance struck between Bre-Ex and Barrick Gold Corp.

The two companies, in a joint submission to the Mines and Energy Ministry, in December agreed to split the property 67.5 percent for Barrick, 22.5 percent for Bre-Ex and the rest to the government. The government has given the parties until February 17 to reach an agreement.
